propositions.text: Applicant seeks judicial review of IAD decision dismissing appeal from ID's Deportation Order.
propositions.quote: Mr. Keith Michael Paul Silvera (the “Applicant”) seeks judicial review of the decision of the Immigration and Refugee Board, Immigration Appeal Division (the “IAD”). In the decision, the IAD dismissed the appeal from a decision of the Immigration and Refugee Board, Immigration Division (the “ID”), issuing a Deportation Order for the Applicant’s removal from Canada to Jamaica.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant seeks judicial review of the IAD decision dismissing his appeal from the ID's Deportation Order, says the court.

propositions.text: Applicant is Jamaican citizen who entered Canada in 1996 as permanent resident sponsored by grandmother.
propositions.quote: The Applicant is a citizen of Jamaica. He entered Canada in 1996 at the age of two years, in the capacity of a permanent resident; his grandmother had sponsored him and his mother.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant is a Jamaican citizen who entered Canada in 1996 as a permanent resident sponsored by his grandmother, says the court.

propositions.text: Applicant convicted in 2018 of indictable offence with potential life sentence, leading to Deportation Order under s.45(d) of IRPA.
propositions.quote: The Applicant was convicted on May 25, 2018, of an indictable offence with a potential sentence of life imprisonment. This conviction led to the issuance of a Deportation Order by the ID, pursuant to subsection 45(d) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, S.C. 2001, c. 27 (the “Act”).

paragraphs.summary: Applicant was convicted in 2018 of an indictable offence, leading to a Deportation Order under s.45(d) of the Act, says the court.

propositions.text: Applicant appealed to IAD under s.63 of the Act, seeking positive discretion on humanitarian and compassionate grounds under s.67(1)(c).
propositions.quote: The Applicant appealed to the IAD, pursuant to section 63 of the Act. He did not challenge the validity of the Deportation Order but sought the positive exercise of discretion pursuant to paragraph 67(1)(c) of the Act, which is on humanitarian and compassionate (“H and C”) grounds.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant appealed to IAD seeking positive discretion on humanitarian and compassionate grounds, not challenging Deportation Order validity, says the court.

propositions.text: IAD referred to Ribic and Chieu decisions setting factors for discretion on humanitarian and compassionate grounds.
propositions.quote: The IAD referred to the decisions in Ribic v. Canada (Minister of Employment and Immigration), [1985] I.A.B.D. No. 4 (Q.L.), and Chieu v. Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), [2002] 1 S.C.R. 84 (S.C.C.), which set out the factors that are relevant to its exercise of discretion on H and C grounds.

paragraphs.summary: The IAD referred to Ribic and Chieu decisions outlining factors for discretion on humanitarian and compassionate grounds, says the earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: IAD decision is reviewable on reasonableness standard per Vavilov.
propositions.quote: The decision of the IAD is reviewable on the standard of reasonableness, pursuant to the decision in Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v. Vavilov, [2019] 4 S.C.R. 653 (S.C.C.).

paragraphs.summary: The IAD decision is reviewable on the reasonableness standard per Vavilov, says the court.

propositions.text: Reasonableness requires decision to show justification, transparency, intelligibility, and be justified by relevant facts and law.
propositions.quote: In considering reasonableness, the Court is to ask if the decision under review "bears the hallmarks of reasonableness — justification, transparency and intelligibility — and whether it is justified in relation to the relevant factual and legal constraints that bear on the decision"; see Vavilov, supra at paragraph 99.

paragraphs.summary: Reasonableness requires the decision to show justification, transparency, intelligibility, and be justified by relevant facts and law, per Vavilov, says the court.

propositions.text: IAD reviewed offence seriousness, rehabilitation possibility, time in Canada, family/community support, and hardship if removed.
propositions.quote: In its decision, the IAD reviewed the seriousness of the offence, the possibility of rehabilitation, the length of time spent by the Applicant in Canada and his establishment, support from his family and the community, and hardship to him if removed to Jamaica. These factors are specifically mentioned in Ribic, supra at pages 4 and 5.

paragraphs.summary: The IAD reviewed offence seriousness, rehabilitation, time in Canada, support, and hardship if removed, says the earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: Applicant is father of four children but did not show his presence is in their best interests.
propositions.quote: The IAD noted that the Applicant is the father of four children, born between 2013 and 2017. It observed that the Applicant had not shown that his presence in their lives is in the best interests of his children.

propositions.text: IAD found some positive factors but significant negatives including escalating criminal behaviour from 2011 to 2018.
propositions.quote: It found that although there were some positive factors in favour of the Applicant, there were significant negative factors, including the history of escalating criminal behaviour from 2011 to 2018.

paragraphs.summary: The IAD found Applicant is father of four but did not prove best interests; noted positive and significant negative factors including escalating criminality, says the earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: Court is not persuaded the IAD decision discloses any reviewable error.
propositions.quote: In light of the evidence before the IAD and the applicable standard of review, I am not persuaded that the decision discloses any reviewable error.

paragraphs.summary: The court is not persuaded the IAD decision discloses any reviewable error, says the court.

propositions.text: Applicant's submissions invite evidence review, which is not the court's role on judicial review.
propositions.quote: The Applicant’s submissions seem to invite a review of the evidence, which is not the role of the Court upon judicial review.

paragraphs.summary: The court says the Applicant's submissions invite evidence review, which is not the court's role on judicial review.

propositions.text: Application for judicial review is dismissed; no question for certification.
propositions.quote: In the result, the application for judicial review will be dismissed, there is no question for certification. JUDGMENT in IMM-7276-21 THIS COURT’S JUDGMENT is that the application for judicial review is dismissed, there is no question for certification.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the application for judicial review and finds no question for certification, says the court.
